## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. 11	- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). **Historical-year expense upload (built, pending release) ✅ DONE:** an **Import Expenses** page at `/expenses/import` (buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from CSV/XLS/XLSX (columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category`; `Tag` ignored; Amount keeps its sign so refunds net). Each row → an imageless `receipts` row (no schema change — `receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` false) + an `expense_categories` link; new category names are auto-created (land Uncategorized, warned in the preview). Two-step **preview → confirm** with count-based dedup (`date|merchant|amount|category`) so re-import is a no-op. Pure `parseExpenseImportCsv` (14) + `computeExpenseImportPlan`/`buildExpenseCategoryLinks` (12) + `ExpenseImportService` (7); the bank-parser CSV primitives were extracted to `csvPrimitives.ts` (base delegates; 229 parser tests unchanged). This **unblocks** prior-period overlay + year-over-year. Deferred: **chart-bar drill-down** (same affordance on the chart bars — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); prior-period overlay + year-over-year (now unblocked), quarter/period selection, multi-chart menu, export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
12	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.

19	## Bugs / UX issues
20	
21	- **Receipt with No Date** - if a receipt has no date it is hard to find in the receipts view.
22	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
23	- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
24	- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which *adds* `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
25	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
26	- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).
27	
28	## Engineering
29	
30	- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.
31	- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
32	- **Expenses list capped at 1000 rows (large imports). ✅ DONE.** `ExpenseService.getExpenses` issued a single PostgREST query with no paging, so Supabase's default 1000-row cap silently truncated the result. After the historical importer added thousands of receipts, the expenses page (which loads all expenses then filters client-side) only held the newest 1000 — a Spending-report drill-down into an older year landed on "No results found — hiding all 1000 expenses", and the Spending report itself undercounted any year over 1000 rows. Fixed by paging `getExpenses` in 1000-row `.range()` batches until a short page (`fetchAllReceiptRows`); the shared Supabase mock gained `range`; 2 new pagination tests in `ExpenseService.getExpenses.spec.ts`. Reported via a `/spending` uncategorized drill-down.
33	- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That's the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the `$page` store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by deriving off the **`$app/state` reactive `page`** object (`import { page } from '$app/state'`; drop the `$`). Apply the same one-line-ish swap to the expenses page (and audit any other `$derived(... $page.url ...)` sites). Not yet reproduced/reported for expenses — latent. See the Spending report design doc and the `$app/state`-in-`$derived` note.
34	- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`supabase/migrations/003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, and again in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert (new migration) and confirm the remote function matches. Found while fixing the email-receipt null-date bug.
35	- **Test the Resend webhook handler. ✅ DONE.** `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` extracted from `Deno.serve` into `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (functional core) with `index.ts` reduced to the dep-wiring shell; `notify.ts` / `mistral.ts` / `exchangeRate.ts` gained optional `fetchFn`/`env` seams. The full branch matrix (rows 1–20: auth gates, body/attachment/fallback flow, notify-on-failure, foreign-currency) is covered in `handler.test.ts` (20 vitest cases, no network/Supabase/Deno). `deno check` clean on all production files. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-resend-handler-testability.md).
36	- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for row 18 (nothing found anywhere), but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case (row 10). The tests assert the real `422` (zero-behaviour-change goal); the PRD table row is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the PRD table or leave the note.
37	- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle (umf1a/2a/3a) was specced but never built. Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.
38	- **Manually verify ReceiptImageViewer gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests only cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
39	- **`npm run lint` is fully green. ✅ DONE.** `npm run lint` (`prettier --check . && eslint .`) passes with exit 0 across the whole repo. Prettier: the repo is clean (`llm_history/`, a chat-log archive, added to `.prettierignore`). ESLint: triaged from 46 → 0. The last 26 were in the Deno edge functions (`supabase/functions/`) and were fixed by typing the payloads rather than relaxing the rule — a `SupabaseClient`/`InsertedReceipt` type alias in `resend/index.ts` + a shared `errText(unknown)` helper (`_shared/errText.ts`, unit-tested), a `RawOcrContent`/typed-env helper + module-scope `toNum(unknown)` in `_shared/mistral.ts`, `content_id?`/`content_disposition?` added to `ResendAttachment`, and the `deno-lint-ignore-file no-explicit-any` directives removed. Verified with `deno check` (both edited source files type-check clean). Note: `deno lint` still reports pre-existing `no-import-prefix` hints on the `https://esm.sh/...` imports — a Deno dependency-management style item, outside the repo's `npm run lint` gate.

41	### Test-coverage backlog
42	
43	Optional, low-priority follow-ups — pure test coverage, no behaviour change.
44	
45	- **Expenses CSV export filename. ✅ DONE.** The inline filter→filename branching moved to `CSVExportService.expenseExportFilename()` (date range wins over category/uncategorized filters; single-category slug + `filtered` fallback preserved) and is unit-tested in `CSVExportService.spec.ts`; the page delegates. Teeth-proven.
46	- **`getSignedReceiptUrl()` edge cases. ✅ DONE.** New `signedUrl.spec.ts` pins the single-path contract: null/empty path → null with no storage call, storage-error → null (never throws), and the expiry (300s OCR / 3600s default) is forwarded to `createSignedUrl`.
47	- **PDF export dimensions & row numbering. ✅ DONE.** `PDFExportService.spec.ts` now loads the generated PDF and asserts every page is US-Letter (612×792), and (via a `drawText` spy) that summary row numbers restart at 1 per category. Both teeth-proven with induced breaks.

See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-resend-handler-testability.md).

51	
52	Tidy the `*.spec.ts` suites. Each item is proven against an oracle or a real induced
53	failure, one spec file per PR-sized unit — see `.scratch/handoff-test-suite-cleanup.md`.

# Backlog

The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
refactoring. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the full
detail (smell, effort, sibling sites, plan) lives in
[Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a reference, not a
separate to-do list.

## Features

- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Client-side pure aggregation (`buildSpendingReport`), view-only, no editing UI. Uncategorized bucket included in Grand Total; refunds (negative amounts) net against spend. **Chart view (v0.60):** `Table | Chart` toggle adds a LayerChart stacked bar (bar per Grouping, stacked by month, sequential ramp; Importance as sub-label; click a bar to drill to Categories, breadcrumb back). Pure `buildSpendingChart`; render-tested. **Table cell drill-down (v0.55) ✅ DONE:** clicking a non-blank table cell opens `/expenses` filtered to exactly what it sums — category×month, category YTD, Grouping/Importance subtotals (expanded to member category ids), Uncategorized (`filter=uncategorized`), and Grand Total (date range only, ties out incl. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). **Historical-year expense upload (built, pending release) ✅ DONE:** an **Import Expenses** page at `/expenses/import` (buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from CSV/XLS/XLSX (columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category`; `Tag` ignored; Amount keeps its sign so refunds net). Each row → an imageless `receipts` row (no schema change — `receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` false) + an `expense_categories` link; new category names are auto-created (land Uncategorized, warned in the preview). Two-step **preview → confirm** with count-based dedup (`date|merchant|amount|category`) so re-import is a no-op. Pure `parseExpenseImportCsv` (14) + `computeExpenseImportPlan`/`buildExpenseCategoryLinks` (12) + `ExpenseImportService` (7); the bank-parser CSV primitives were extracted to `csvPrimitives.ts` (base delegates; 229 parser tests unchanged). This **unblocks** prior-period overlay + year-over-year. Deferred: **chart-bar drill-down** (same affordance on the chart bars — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); prior-period overlay + year-over-year (now unblocked), quarter/period selection, multi-chart menu, export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account.
- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it.
- **iPhone camera.** Use the Camera app on iPhone to take photos of receipts.
- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y _(optional UX, low priority)_.** Recent-categories dropdown section (exp2b), mobile-responsive category dropdown (exp8a), and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support (exp8b) were specced but never built.
- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits _(optional, low priority)_.** Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (vca2a email path) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal (fcr2b) were specced but not implemented.

## Bugs / UX issues

- **Receipt with No Date** - if a receipt has no date it is hard to find in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which *adds* `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

## Engineering

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
- **Expenses list capped at 1000 rows (large imports). ✅ DONE.** `ExpenseService.getExpenses` issued a single PostgREST query with no paging, so Supabase's default 1000-row cap silently truncated the result. After the historical importer added thousands of receipts, the expenses page (which loads all expenses then filters client-side) only held the newest 1000 — a Spending-report drill-down into an older year landed on "No results found — hiding all 1000 expenses", and the Spending report itself undercounted any year over 1000 rows. Fixed by paging `getExpenses` in 1000-row `.range()` batches until a short page (`fetchAllReceiptRows`); the shared Supabase mock gained `range`; 2 new pagination tests in `ExpenseService.getExpenses.spec.ts`. Reported via a `/spending` uncategorized drill-down.
- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That's the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the `$page` store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by deriving off the **`$app/state` reactive `page`** object (`import { page } from '$app/state'`; drop the `$`). Apply the same one-line-ish swap to the expenses page (and audit any other `$derived(... $page.url ...)` sites). Not yet reproduced/reported for expenses — latent. See the Spending report design doc and the `$app/state`-in-`$derived` note.
- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`supabase/migrations/003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, and again in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert (new migration) and confirm the remote function matches. Found while fixing the email-receipt null-date bug.
- **Test the Resend webhook handler. ✅ DONE.** `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` extracted from `Deno.serve` into `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (functional core) with `index.ts` reduced to the dep-wiring shell; `notify.ts` / `mistral.ts` / `exchangeRate.ts` gained optional `fetchFn`/`env` seams. The full branch matrix (rows 1–20: auth gates, body/attachment/fallback flow, notify-on-failure, foreign-currency) is covered in `handler.test.ts` (20 vitest cases, no network/Supabase/Deno). `deno check` clean on all production files. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-resend-handler-testability.md).
- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for row 18 (nothing found anywhere), but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case (row 10). The tests assert the real `422` (zero-behaviour-change goal); the PRD table row is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the PRD table or leave the note.
- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle (umf1a/2a/3a) was specced but never built. Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.
- **Manually verify ReceiptImageViewer gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests only cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
- **`npm run lint` is fully green. ✅ DONE.** `npm run lint` (`prettier --check . && eslint .`) passes with exit 0 across the whole repo. Prettier: the repo is clean (`llm_history/`, a chat-log archive, added to `.prettierignore`). ESLint: triaged from 46 → 0. content.text:
`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

Done. I replaced the separate bulk control with the behavior you suggested.

## What changed

**Removed** the "Set category for N selected: [dropdown]" toolbar element entirely.

**Now:** when you have multiple rows checked, picking a category on **any selected row's own category dropdown** applies it to the whole selection — one batched `bulkAssignCategory` upsert, then the selection clears and a toast confirms ("Set 10 expenses to …").

The branch logic in `handleCategorySelect`:
- Row is in a multi-row selection (`selected.has(receiptId) && size > 1`) → fan out to all selected, no vendor rule (spans many merchants).
- Otherwise (nothing selected, or just that one row) → unchanged single-row path, which keeps the vendor-rule auto-creation.

**Discoverability:** since the fan-out is otherwise invisible, I kept one passive, non-interactive hint line that shows only while >1 row is selected: *"Pick a category on any selected row to set all 10."* It's not a control — but if you'd rather have nothing there, say so and I'll drop it.

- `npm run check`: 0 errors / 0 warnings
- Full unit suite: **1402 passed, 8 skipped**

- Tests updated: the old toolbar-picker test became a **fan-out** test, plus a new **single-row guard** test proving an unselected row still uses the single path (and doesn't call `bulkAssignCategory`)

content.text:
Done. Unassigned categories in `/spending/hierarchy` now show their expense count after the name.

## What I did

- **`HierarchyEditor.svelte`** — new optional `expenseCounts?: Record<string, number>` prop; each unassigned category renders `Name (N)` (the count in a muted amber `data-testid="category-count"` span). A category missing from the map shows no count, so it degrades cleanly.
- **`spending/hierarchy/+page.svelte`** — in `load()`, after building the tree, it fetches an exact head-count (`CategoryService.countCategoryExpenses`, no 1000-row cap) for **just the unassigned categories**, in parallel. A failed count is skipped rather than failing the page, and counts refresh on every mutation (assign/delete/rename) since `load()` reruns.

So e.g. "Mystery Spend (3)" — the number of expenses currently sitting in that unassigned category.

**Scope note:** I applied this only to the *unassigned* bucket, as you asked. It'd be a one-line change to also show counts on grouped categories if you want that later — say the word.

**Verification**
- `npm run check`: 0 errors / 0 warnings
- Full unit suite: **1404 passed, 8 skipped** (+2 new render tests: count shown, count omitted)
- ESLint + Prettier clean on touched files

I verified the component render via tests but didn't drive the live page (needs an authenticated/seeded session, which there's no harness for). The page wiring is straightforward and typechecks. Changes are staged, not committed.
